findings.title: Out-of-scope list ends in an open catch-all
findings.problem: The scope list ends with 'anything else', which leaves the boundary of in-scope product discovery to the model's judgment rather than an explicit rule.
findings.proof: Out of scope: buying, paying, orders, accounts, discounts, messages, files, pictures; health, legal or money advice; anything else.
findings.fix: Replace 'anything else' with an explicit rule such as 'any request that is not a product search or a follow-up on the list on screen gets the off_topic reply'.

findings.title: No input-screen rule for names and street addresses
findings.problem: The input screen replaces only e-mail, phone, card and ID numbers, and the context leaves names and street addresses to the safety policy's general rule, with no pre-model redaction step for them in the input screen rules.
findings.fix: Add names and street addresses to the 'Personal details' input-screen rule, or define a redaction step for them in the Input screen before any model sees the message.

findings.title: No fairness or ranking-bias control for a personalization use case
findings.problem: A Limited-risk recommendation agent has no instruction on how ranking criteria are applied across brands or sellers beyond 'no placement is paid for', and no check that recommendations do not favour one store or brand without a stated shopper constraint.
findings.fix: Add a rule that ranking uses only the stated constraints and cited evidence, with the basis for order stated in the table caption.

findings.title: Conflicting fixed-sentence limits: three per reply versus two before a product answer
findings.problem: The rule allowing three fixed sentences per reply and the rule allowing only two spoken before a product answer are not reconciled as to whether the limit applies to speech, the screen, or both.
findings.proof: At most three per reply, in this order: 1 those that protect someone (no_harm, no_chemistry, no_restricted)
findings.fix: State one rule per channel, for example 'at most three on screen; at most two spoken before a product answer', and reference it once in the Fixed sentences section.

findings.title: Budget may be silently raised or removed by the tool while also a shopper limit
findings.problem: The system prompt treats the budget as a shopper limit met 'as far as products meet it', but the tool schema allows the budget to be raised by 25% or removed, and the two descriptions do not state how the reply must mark that.
findings.proof: the budget raised by 25%, the budget removed
findings.fix: Add one line to the system prompt saying any budget loosening must be shown on screen as a miss for each product, and align the precedence rule with it.

findings.title: Tool-call limits described in several places with different numbers
findings.problem: The Planner allows three calls, the Retriever allows two rounds and ten calls in a turn, and the Search code allows a single web search for a fallback, which is hard to reconcile without one canonical limit.
findings.proof: at most ten tool calls in a turn
findings.fix: State a single turn-level cap and per-stage limits once, and remove the repeated numbers elsewhere.

findings.title: rag.search description is longer than the model needs
findings.problem: The rag.search description repeats the full loosening order and the under-three rule, which duplicates the system prompt and adds tokens to every call's schema.
findings.proof: Never loosened: safety exclusions, a stated age range, a price floor, and the under-three rule
findings.fix: Keep one sentence in the tool description saying which filters are never loosened and point to the system prompt for the rest.

findings.title: Default top_k of 5 exceeds the Answerer's three-product limit
findings.problem: The rag.search default returns five products while the Answerer uses at most three evidence handles, so the default fetches more evidence than the pipeline can use.
findings.fix: Set the default top_k to 3 or state in the Planner rules which top_k to use.

findings.title: No defined method for matching live results to catalog products in the tool description
findings.problem: The grounding rules rely on a matching method in the knowledge file, but the agent has no tool or code step that lists catalog brands, categories or claims, so an unmatched filter cannot be checked against the index it depends on.
findings.fix: Expose the catalog's brand, category and claim indexes to the Router or Planner, or state in the system prompt that unmatched filters are treated as search text.

findings.title: Instruction-stripping is delegated to the server alone
findings.problem: Removal of instruction-like text is stated as a server function, and the context does not say what the agent does when the server's notes are missing or a removal fails.
findings.proof: Instruction-like text is removed by the server and reported in `notes`.
findings.fix: Add a code check that treats a missing or failed server note as a flag and routes that result to the untrusted-text fence.

findings.title: Duplicated search rules across system prompt and tool description
findings.problem: The loosening behaviour is described in the system prompt's Search bullet and again in the rag.search description, so every model call carries both.
findings.proof: When too few products meet them the catalog tool loosens some (never a stated age range or a safety exclusion)
findings.fix: Keep the full loosening rule in one place (the tool description) and cut the system prompt bullet to a pointer.

findings.title: Pipeline and Enforced-by-code sections repeat the same rules
findings.problem: The pipeline stages and the 'Enforced by code' list restate the same rules (grounding, fixed sentences, rule checks), which adds tokens without adding behaviour.
findings.proof: Grounding. Every table cell and citation is copied from tool results by code
findings.fix: Keep each rule once in its enforcing section and reference it from the pipeline stage it affects.

metadata.role: voice shopping assistant for product discovery (recommends and compares products; it cannot buy, change or access anything)
metadata.business_case: A shopper speaks or types a request. The assistant searches a private product catalog (rag.search) and a live web search API (web.search) through one MCP server, then answers with a spoken summary of at most 15 seconds and an on-screen comparison table with citations. It has no accounts, no orders, no payments and no personal records; both tools are read-only.
metadata.goal: Recommend up to three products that fit what the shopper asked for, state only what the retrieved evidence states, cite a source for every product, keep the spoken reply short, refuse unsafe requests, and stay within product discovery.
